title: The Weeping Wax Saint
text: One morning a saint of wax stands in the square, weeping real tears. Pilgrims come from three valleys. So do the flies, and the flies are wrong: each has a tiny human face.

options.label: Let the pilgrims come, and take their coin for the Commons.

outcomes.text: Candles and coin fill the square. The saint weeps on, and the flies stay close to it.
The saint's face softens a little each day. One morning it wears the face of a Scion of the city, who has felt watched ever since.

options.label: Melt the wax saint down, and learn what is inside it.

outcomes.text: The wax screams as it runs. In the pool at the bottom is a human skull, old and gilded. The faithful do not forgive it.
The wax will not melt. The fire under it does not go out for three days, and takes a House's outbuilding with it.

options.label: Sell it to the Apostate traders, who have asked twice, and let them carry it off.

outcomes.text: They pay well and ask nothing. The flies follow the cart out of the city, and then, one by one, come back.
